purpose: Accuracy, stability and single-thread speed of RapidGLM against the standard R and Python GLM fitters, and its drop-in interfaces.
reference: Damped Newton in IEEE binary128 (benchmarks/glm/reference.cpp); NB theta by profile bisection over [1e-6, 1e8].
accuracy_scope: Problems with a finite, identifiable MLE, excluding relative collinearity 1e-12 (aliased by R's threshold). Failure: error, missing identifiable coefficient, or coefficient error above 1e-3 reference standard errors.

speed_scope: Minimum over up to seven repeats (15 s budget) of a fit on loaded in-memory data, one efficiency core, one BLAS/OpenMP thread. Every tool/problem command starts after the retained quiet predicate. Tool defaults unless marked tight; waits are excluded.

environment.note: One workstation: Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB RAM; BIOS 1836, microcode 0x133, 253 W sustained and short-term limits; 4 x 32 GiB at 4,200 MT/s. Turbo is on. Two faulty performance cores (logical CPUs 8-11) are capped at 2.2 GHz and never used for timing. Every timed run is pinned to the 16 identical efficiency cores, one thread per core, under the shared lock after a quiet-host check. Pinning to identical cores makes the comparisons reproducible. The efficiency cores retain their stock 800 MHz-4.3 GHz range. Absolute seconds from other host settings are not directly comparable; use matched speed-up ratios across settings. These timings are final, not provisional. Final timings on the 16 identical efficiency cores (CPUs 16-31), one thread per core: one on 16, four on 16-19, eight on 16-23, twelve on 16-27, sixteen on 16-31. Each timed command holds the shared lock and starts after two consecutive ten-second quiet samples: one-minute load <=4 and every selected CPU <20% busy. Both samples are retained. Untimed work uses CPUs 0-7 under nice 10. These release timings are final, not provisional.
